24 Two electromagnetic waves have wavelengths of 5.0 × 10–7
m and 5.0 × 10–2
m.
Which row identifies the regions of the electromagnetic spectrum to which the waves belong?
wavelength
5.0 × 10–7
m
wavelength
5.0 × 10–2
m
A
ultraviolet
infrared
B
visible
microwave
C
ultraviolet
microwave
D
visible
infrared

hints: Convert the first wavelength to nanometres: $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 500 \text{ nm}$ and compare it with the visible range of about $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$.
Recall the order of increasing wavelength around this part of the spectrum: ultraviolet, then visible, then infrared, then microwave.
Convert the second wavelength to centimetres: $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m} = 5.0 \text{ cm}$ and compare it with the infrared limit of about $1 \text{ mm}$.
walkthrough: Write the two given wavelengths with convenient units: $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 500 \text{ nm}$ and $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m} = 5.0 \text{ cm} = 50 \text{ mm}$.
Recall that visible light covers roughly $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, while ultraviolet has shorter wavelength than about $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Since $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ is between $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, it belongs to visible light.
Recall that infrared extends from about $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ up to about $1 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, and longer wavelengths up to about $1 \text{ m}$ are microwaves.
Since $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ is much larger than $1 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, it belongs to microwaves, not infrared.
The pair visible plus microwave matches the row for $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ is too long for ultraviolet and $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ is too long for infrared.

B.explanation: $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ lies in the visible range and $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ lies in the microwave range.

C.explanation: $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ is microwave, but $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ is visible light, not ultraviolet.

D.explanation: $5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ is visible light, but $5.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ is microwave, not infrared.
